messages:
ravi: Heads-up — PR gates started failing intermittently for the quantize-onboard pipeline. Most failures look like runner startup / artifact pull timeouts rather than test logic.
emily: saw this too. failing logs show long docker image pulls and model artifact downloads ~10-20m each. PRs with big matrix blow past the 60m job window. example log snippet:
```\nError: Job exceeded maximum duration of 60 minutes\nStep: pull_model_artifact -> timed out after 1200s\n```
sam: ouch. are these GH Actions self-hosted runners? or hosted? that changes the fix.
maya: 99% self-hosted (our gpu pool autoscaler). it's flapping during peak PR traffic. cold nodes + model downloads = bad combo. also quantized model builds add extra startup work.
ravi: current GH Actions YAML uses a large matrix for model variants (float16, int8, int4) x dataset shards x batch sizes. that's >30 jobs for a PR sometimes. here's the relevant bit:
```yaml\nstrategy:\n  matrix:\n    quant: [fp16, int8, int4]\n    shard: [s0, s1, s2, s3]\n  fail-fast: false\n```
emily: for PR gating we only need a smoke pass. can we reduce matrix to one representative quant and one shard, then run full matrix in nightly Buildkite? that should cut queue pressure and reduce cold starts.
sam: agreed. propose two immediate changes: 1) make PR workflow a lightweight smoke job limited to 1 quant x 1 shard; 2) move heavy matrix runs to nightly Buildkite (where runners are larger and provisioned). also prewarm runners by pre-pulling docker + model cache.
maya: autoscaler health is tracked but we need warm pool. infra can add a small reserved warm pool for PR window. but we should also avoid wasting GPU credits. alternately we can prefetch artifacts into a shared cache bucket and mount on runner.
ci-bot: reminder — rate limit to the model artifact S3 bucket was raised last week; that may have shifted more load to runner downloads.
ravi: concrete quick fixes I can do this sprint:
- PR gate -> smoke.yaml: reduce matrix to `quant: [fp16]` `shard: [s0]` and add an early smoke test set.
- add a pre-pull step to actions that tries a cached model tarball on a fast HTTP store, fallback to S3 only if missing.
- add `timeout-minutes: 90` to long-running nightly jobs only, not PRs.
emily: for the pre-pull step, we could use our CDN-fronted cache path: `https://artifacts.redwood/fast-cache/` — it's gzipped tarballs of quantized artifacts.
sam: another low-risk option: gate only on unit-tests + a tiny end-to-end smoke eval (100 tokens) and run full evals as a required status check but not blocking PR (i.e., mark as `non-blocking` in branch protection). that keeps velocity while surfacing regressions.
maya: I'll schedule an infra change to keep 2 warm GPU nodes between 9a-6p PT on weekdays for PR windows. i'll also add jitter and backoff to the autoscaler so we don't spin too many nodes at once.
ravi: also found a subtle failure mode: our GA runner label selection falls back to hosted if `self-hosted` label absent, but the workflow uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, gpu]` and the matrix expands causing some jobs to land on tiny hosted runners that can't handle docker layers -> silent long pulls. recommend explicit `runs-on: self-hosted && gpu-large` or use `if: runner == 'gpu-large'` gating.
emily: good call — i'll update the workflow to explicit runner labels and add an assertion step to fail fast if runner lacks `/dev/nvidia0`.
sam: for longer term: 1) shift heavy quantization builds to a dedicated Buildkite pipeline with pinned `gpu-large` executors, 2) cache model shards in a shared NFS on the infra side for fast local mounts, 3) add a small smoke dataset & metric that runs in <5m for PR gating.
ci-bot: plan created: PR-smoke -> 1719234600, Buildkite-heavy migration -> 1719239000, infra warm pool -> 1719242000.
ravi: assigning tasks: @emily -> GH Actions smoke workflow patch; @maya -> infra warm pool + autoscaler jitter; @sam -> Buildkite pipeline skeleton; I'll own the pre-pull cache + workflow labels.
emily: will open a small PR for smoke.yaml and pre-pull step this morning. pinging @maya for the cache URL.
maya: I'll provision a 2-node warm pool and add cache rules. ETA EOD today.
sam: I'll scaffold the Buildkite pipeline and add an initial nightly schedule that runs the full quant matrix on a rolling shard distribution.
ravi: thanks all. once smoke gating is in, let's monitor flakes for 48h and then iterate. adding a low-priority follow-up to consider switching PR gating to Cirrus-style ephemeral warm pools if this keeps recurring. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: note: created ticket INFRA-1542 for warm-pool and CI-3124 for GH Actions smoke gating.
